business_summary: Cboe Global Markets, Inc. (Cboe: CBOE) is an exchange holding company. It holds two sourced roles on this chain from a single March 2026 announcement: prediction-market-venue (planning Mini-SPX prediction-market contracts listed on Cboe Options Exchange) and clearing-and-collateral (those contracts route into OCC clearing, with Cboe as listing exchange rather than the DCO itself).

exposure_summary.narrative: Cboe holds two sourced roles on prediction-market-plumbing: prediction-market-venue (CROWDED, chain position 7) and clearing-and-collateral (EMERGING, position 8), both resting on Cboe's planned Mini-SPX contract, an options wrapper rather than a binary event contract, using OCC as the clearing utility rather than a new DCO. FY2025 revenue was USD 4,714.2M (6.0% three-year CAGR) with a 31.1% operating margin, net income of USD 1,100.0M, and clean quality (Piotroski 9/9 STRONG). Net debt to EBITDA is -0.93x, a net-cash position. Beneish is PENDING_DATA this run: companyfacts is missing sga_fy for this filer (11/12 inputs found).

crowdedness_caveats: prediction-market-venue is scored CROWDED, not EMERGING: the chain notes five listed issuers (ICE via Polymarket, DraftKings via Railbird, IBKR via ForecastEx, CME via FanDuel, Cboe via an options wrapper) have already reached this seat, and the two largest venues by volume, Kalshi and Polymarket, are private, which the chain calls the crowdedness trap on this link.

Cboe's approach is structurally distinct from the other prediction-market-venue issuer profiled this batch (ICE): an options wrapper cleared through OCC rather than a CFTC-designated contract market or introducing-broker structure.
